baseNote.text:
Agreed for both: Home = Continue at the top, then your whole library with Import; sidebar with Library filters, Paths and Collections; a mini-player with back 15, play/pause and forward 15.

A = covers in a grid, each with a bar that fills as you read.
B = a shelf of spines; each spine fills from the bottom as you read.

B in dark: select the board, Tweaks, theme = dark.

Books, notes and numbers are samples, not your real library.

c4Note.text:
One question on Home

One question from the question bank of a chapter you marked wrong, to recall before you read on (retrieval practice: recalling a fact strengthens memory more than rereading it).

Uses: question banks and your right/wrong marks (M6). Needs the Claude key on the live site to have questions at all.

c5Note.text:
Threads across books

Two of your highlights from different books that share key words, shown together.

Uses: the cross-book matcher (M6), which compares word stems, not AI. It finds shared words, so some threads will be weak.

continueNote.text:
A = plain: cover, title, chapter and a fill bar.
B = also shows your last note (or highlight) in that book, and offers Read from here or Listen from here, both starting at the same paragraph.

pathNote.text:
A Path has a reading order (story first, then the deeper book). Every title says what you can do with it: Read and listen, Read only, Listen only, or Not available yet. A title with nothing to read or listen to yet is greyed, and takes its colour when you add the book or audio.

Corrected from the 2026-10-03 prototype: in How systems fail, Meltdown is the story (N) and Normal Accidents the deeper book (E), as in your reading list.

Only one layout so far; say if you want options here too.

playerNote.text:
All three have back 15 s, play/pause and forward 15 s, on desktop and phone.

A = compact, like Apple Books; a thin line along the bottom fills with the chapter.
B = shows the sentence being read, with the word lit; Go to the page; Think aloud records a voice note on that sentence.
C = a scrubber you can drag, times, speed (1.0×) and Think aloud.

progressNote.text:
No ribbon, as you asked: progress is a fill.

A = a bar under the cover fills (what the app does today).
B = the cover fills with a lighter tone from the bottom.
C = the spine fills with amber from the bottom.

Kept on all three: folded corner = your notes; headphones = audio to read along; amber tick = finished.

picksNote.text:
Your picks, drawn together:

Home on desktop: A, covers in a grid.
Home on a phone: A, with a Grid / Spines toggle.
Mini-player: B (the sentence being read) plus a speed you choose.
Progress: A, a bar under the cover fills.
Continue: B, your last note, Read from here / Listen from here.
Every title is labelled by what is available: Read and listen, Read only, Listen only, or Not available yet (greyed). Fabless shows the last one.

The option boards below are kept for reference. Dark: select a board, Tweaks, theme = dark (the player board shows both).

rowAccount.text: Decided (2026-10-06): the account button on a phone, B

accountNote.text:
On a phone there is no sidebar, so Reading stats, Your data, Invite and Sign out sit behind a round button with your initial (S).

A = a strip at the top of every page (what the app does today). Always one tap; every page loses about 68 px of height.
B = the button sits on Home only, beside Import. Every other page starts straight with its title. From another page: tap Home, then S.
C = the button in every page's own title row. Always one tap, no strip; every page's header carries it.

Samuel chose B on 2026-10-06 (Claude's recommendation: it is your Phone A mockup, and these links are rarely used).

Dark: select the board, Tweaks, theme = dark.
Books and numbers are samples.
